<!-- Generated by `make docs-gen` from the code. Do not edit: change the code and regenerate. -->

Asks one of your models about the items it receives, all together, and puts each item's answer on it, with the model's name, its version and the worker. A model with no worker connected fails at once.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `data.ask` |
| Kind | Node |
| Inputs | `main` |
| Outputs | `main` |

Items that fail stop the execution, unless **Continue on failure** is on: then they leave on the `error` port instead. What fails is tried again only when **Retry** asks.

## Settings

| Setting | Kind | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model (`model`) | model | yes |  | The model asked: one of yours, on Data → Models. Personal: sharing the workflow leaves it out. |
| Fields (`fields`) | list of text | no |  | The fields each item sends, like city or outcomes.0.price, each under its name as written; none for the whole item. Each names a field of the items it receives; saving checks the items have it. |
| Answer schema (`schema`) | text | no |  | A JSON Schema each answer keeps to, which the model is told: an answer that does not fails its item. Empty for any JSON. |
| Answer field (`field`) | text | no | `prediction` | Where the answer goes on the item. |
| Wait (`wait`) | duration, e.g. `30s`, `5m`, `1h` | no | `30s` | How long to wait for the answers, up to the instance's most: 5 minutes unless an admin says. |

## Items

The items it receives, passed on with these fields added, `prediction` under the name **Answer field** (`field`) gives. Decimals are text, so they stay exact; times are RFC 3339 text.

| Field | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `prediction` | object | The model's answer for the item. |
| `prediction.answer` | anything | Its answer: any JSON, as the model gave it. |
| `prediction.model` | text | The model's name. |
| `prediction.version` | text; not always there | The version its worker or URL said it was. |
| `prediction.worker` | text; not always there | The worker that answered, for a worker model. |
